inconsistencies: Duplicate work: #35322 and #35355 both replace the mutex-protected log-level map with atomic category bitmasks to make disabled-log checks lock-free. Only one should land; #35322 is standalone while #35355 is stacked on #34038.

Competing approaches to the same problem: #34038 (replace -loglevel with -trace plus RPC) and #35387 (make -loglevel work standalone plus a new loglevel RPC) both fix trace-logging configuration ergonomics. Review #34038 first — #35355 pulls from it and #34730 is explicitly blocked on it.

Settings chain, order matters: #16545 → #17580 → #17493 → #17581, with #17783 stacked on #16545+#17580. The cards also conflict about the base: #31260 claims to be the foundation for #16545, while #16545 claims to be the foundation for the follow-ups. Reviewers should settle which is the base before working the stack.
#36861 adds ad-hoc range validation to numeric options, overlapping the typed-settings infrastructure of #16545/#31260. Coordinate so the same checks are not implemented twice in incompatible ways.
util::Result chain: #25665 is the base for #26022, #25722 (which also needs #26022) and #29700. Read #25665 first; the three dependents only make sense after it.
Logging chain: #34778 → #29256 → #30342 (and the out-of-category #30343). #34778 must be reviewed before the two PRs it carries.
#36087 introduces AssertUnreachable and #35911 is built on it to enable -Wmissing-noreturn; review #36087 first.

#29491 and #36122 both vendor unmerged, experimental libsecp256k1 modules; neither can be finalized before the corresponding upstream work, and a shared decision on vendoring experimental modules would cover both.
#27409 changes default datadir resolution (symlinks/redirect files) and #36373 logs the symlink-resolved datadir; #27409 should be settled first since it defines what the resolved path means.
#35688 and #36812 both modify CHMAC_SHA256 internals (empty-key handling vs cached state copy) and will touch the same code.
result.notes: The category as assessed had no P1 at all despite containing two defects in core primitives (an observed std::terminate on disk-full in stream writing, and an out-of-bounds read in the JSON tokenizer); those two were raised so the band is used for what it is defined for. The P2 band is large but genuinely heterogeneous: user-visible configuration and datadir bugs, two security hardenings, two measured crypto speedups, and the two infrastructure stacks (typed settings, util::Result/logging macros) that several other listed PRs depend on. Several entries here (silent payments, parallel index sync, loadtxoutset, cpu_load) are mainly other areas' work counted in utils only for the shared primitive they introduce; they are ranked on that primitive, not on the feature.
